title: Bilevel optimization with nonunique lower minimizers: uniform perturbed PL conditions and exact gradients.
summary: Consider the optimistic bilevel problem $Y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}g(x,y)$, $\Phi(x)=\min_{y\in Y^*(x)}f(x,y)$, and seek stationarity of $\min_x\Phi(x)$. Multiple global lower-level solutions are allowed; the defining minima must be attained. Among lower-level minimizers, select one minimizing the upper-level objective.

description_paragraphs: Consider the optimistic bilevel problem $Y^*(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^{d_y}}g(x,y)$, $\Phi(x)=\min_{y\in Y^*(x)}f(x,y)$, and seek stationarity of $\min_x\Phi(x)$. Multiple global lower-level solutions are allowed; the defining minima must be attained. Among lower-level minimizers, select one minimizing the upper-level objective.

model.instance: (f,g,x0,y0) and declared oracle law; dimensions are arbitrary finite and minimax is over them

assumptions.description: For every x and $t\in[0,\bar t]$, the lower-level minimum of $h_t=g+tf$ is finite and attained, and $\|\nabla_yh_t\|^2\ge2\mu(h_t-\min_yh_t)$ holds globally with the same mu for all x,t. This includes g at t=0 but does not follow from g being PL alone. Strong convexity and uniqueness are not required.
The function f is C_f-Lipschitz in the lower-level variable y, uniformly in x. Convexity in x and global value-Lipschitz continuity in x are not assumed.
The full gradient of $f$ is jointly $L_f$-Lipschitz in $(x,y)$, and its full Hessian is jointly $\rho_f$-Lipschitz. The constant $L$ is a common upper bound on $L_f$ and $L_g$.
The full gradient of $g$ is jointly $L_g$-Lipschitz in $(x,y)$, and its full Hessian is jointly $\rho_g=\rho$-Lipschitz. Strong convexity of g is not additionally assumed.
The optimistic objective satisfies $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$, with Delta a public fixed finite initialization budget.

The initial point satisfies $\operatorname{dist}(y_0,Y^*(x_0))\le R_0$, with z0 = y0. The source solution-set perturbation bound gives an initial tracking bound from public data. Distance is measured to the solution set; no undeclared unique y* is selected.

bounds.derivation:
Let $v_t$ be the computed hypergradient surrogate, $\eta>0$ the step size, and $\bar\delta_t\ge0$ a publicly computable tracking-error bound. Choose public constants $a,c\ge0$ and bias budget $B\ge0$ satisfying
$$
\begin{aligned}
\|v_t-\nabla\Phi(x_t)\|&\le\sqrt{a\bar\delta_t}+B,\\
\bar\delta_{t+1}&=\tfrac12\bar\delta_t+c\eta^2\|v_t\|^2,\\
C_t&=\|v_t\|+\sqrt{a\bar\delta_t}+B.
\end{aligned}
$$
Then $C_t$ is a computable upper bound on the true gradient norm. Define $t_* = \min\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{0\le t<T} C_t$, break ties by the smallest index, and return $x_{t_*}$. Under $\eta\le(2L_\Phi)^{-1}$, $ac\eta^2\le1/16$, and $a\le1/\eta$, summing the descent inequalities and the tracking recurrence gives
$$
\min_{t<T}C_t^2\le\frac{27\Delta/\eta+60a\bar\delta_0}{T}+30B^2.
$$
The choices $B\le\varepsilon/\sqrt{60}$ and $T\ge(54\Delta/\eta+120a\bar\delta_0)/\varepsilon^2$ therefore ensure $\|\nabla\Phi(x_{t_*})\|\le\varepsilon$ deterministically. The public initialization budget determines $\bar\delta_0$. Increasing the constants in the inner iteration counts and the existing logarithmic factors enforces these conditions without changing the stated query order. Selection uses only the surrogate and scalar recurrence, with no query to the true hypergradient.
